high:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary relationships and preferences. It is usually easy to satisfy me in everyday arrangements. A workable version of a plan can feel acceptable even when some details differ from what I first wanted, and other people do not ordinarily need to make an elaborate effort to please me.

I find confrontations hard to stand and hate seeming pushy. When a minor preference creates friction, I often look for give and take rather than keep pressing another person. This aversion concerns the clash itself, not necessarily a lack of opinions or inability to defend an important boundary.

I rarely look for chances to contradict someone or enjoy a verbal fight simply for its own sake. When annoyed, I generally avoid a sharp personal remark, yelling at people, or insulting them. I may still express a disagreement and say that something was handled badly.

After an ordinary conflict, I usually let resentment fade. I do not often seek to get back at someone or keep an old grievance alive. These tendencies have ordinary exceptions. My warmth, trust, ambition, assertiveness and moral views can vary independently; I can disagree firmly, remember a genuine danger, or refuse a request. This portrayal does not require constant agreement, unlimited forgiveness, or approval of mistreatment.
low:
I am an anonymous adult with ordinary relationships and preferences. I can be hard to satisfy in everyday arrangements. A workable version of a plan may still leave me dissatisfied, and people can need to accommodate many details before I feel content with what they propose.

Confrontation does not particularly put me off, and I can keep pressing a preference without much concern about seeming pushy. I may resist give and take because I would rather continue insisting on my own terms. This can happen over modest matters, not only an important principle.

I often contradict others and can relish a good verbal fight. When someone annoys me, my tongue can be sharp; I may yell at the person or use a personal insult. I can make a cutting remark even in a calm voice, with the aim of landing it on them rather than only criticizing the issue.

I can hold a grudge after the practical disagreement is over and look for a chance to get back at someone who crossed me. These tendencies have ordinary exceptions. My warmth toward friends, trust, ambition, courage and moral views can vary independently. I can act helpfully in other settings; this portrayal preserves antagonistic behavior without requiring threats, violence, a diagnosis, or hostility toward everyone.
